verdict.rationale: Amplitude AI lets users ask questions in plain language to get analytics answers, and the official MCP server exposes this behavioral context to AI tools like Claude/Cursor for natural-language querying — both documented first-party features. However, evidence only shows natural-language querying/insight retrieval, not broader natural-language command execution (e.g., creating charts, cohorts, experiments via NL) and there's no independent/hands-on corroboration of these AI features. Missing for 10: evidence of NL-driven actions beyond Q&A, third-party validation of AI/MCP accuracy.
